text.p01: To those who tells the truth like Riley A Story about Truth
text.p03: In a bustling city, under the glow of streetlights, lived a little raccoon named Riley.
text.p05: Always exploring alleyways and rooftops with bright eyes and nimble paws.
text.p06: One evening, Riley met a wise old pigeon named Maggie. She had seen the city change and grow.
text.p07: “Why do you always look so calm, Maggie?” Riley asked. “Aren’t you ever scared of getting into trouble?”
text.p08: Maggie fluffed his feathers and smiled. “Trouble comes and goes, little one. But the truth? It stays with you.”
text.p09: Riley tilted his head. “But what if telling the truth makes things worse?” Maggie replied “Truth will always set you free. It might be hard at first, but it opens doors lies never can.”
text.p10: Riley thought about Maggie’s words as he scampered through the city streets with his best friend Benny.
text.p11: Benny was big and strong, always ready to protect Riley when things got tricky.
text.p12: One chilly evening, they smelled something delicious —freshly baked bread!
text.p13: The scent led them to a small bakery with an open window, and their noses twitched with excitement.
text.p14: “Let’s take a peek,” whispered Benny. They climbed inside, their paws soft against the floor.
text.p15: They found sweet rolls on the counter, warm and inviting. They couldn’t resist nibbling on the treats.
text.p16: But then —CRASH! Riley’s tail knocked over a tray. The noise echoed through the baker
text.p17: The baker woke up with a start!
text.p18: The baker rushed in and found the two raccoons frozen in place. “Who made this mess?” he shouted.
text.p19: Benny whispered, “I’ll take the blame. I’m bigger. I can handle it, you can go.”
text.p20: Riley’s heart pounded. Benny was trying to protect him
text.p21: but Riley remembered what Maggie had said: “Truth will always set you free.”
text.p22: Riley took a deep breath and stepped forward. “It was me who did it,” he admitted.
text.p23: “We were just hungry and curious. I’m sorry.” Benny looked surprised but stayed quiet.
text.p24: The baker frowned, his eyes narrowing. But then he saw the honesty in Riley’s eyes.
text.p25: “You’re brave for telling the truth,” he said. “Next time, just ask. I’ll leave some treats outside for you.”
text.p26: The baker shooed them out, but Riley felt lighter, even proud.
text.p27: Benny looked at him in surprise. “Why did you tell the truth? I could’ve taken the blame.”
text.p28: Riley smiled. “Because lying only traps you in more lies. But the truth? It set me free.”
text.p29: From that day on, Riley was known as the Honest Little Raccoon.
text.p30: The city felt brighter, and Riley’s heart felt free, knowing that truth had opened more than just the baker’s door
text.p31: —it had opened his own heart too.
